name: @cloudsforge/pool
description: Stratum v1 mining pool for the Bitcoin-family chains the estate runs its own nodes for: getblocktemplate, vardiff, share validation and PPLNS accounting.
_runtimeDependencies: The @cloudsforge/* runtime packages and @cloudsforge/contracts-chain are consumed as file:
paths because they are not published yet. Once AD-02 lands they become registry versions and
these paths — plus the two named build contexts in the Dockerfile and the extra checkouts in
CI — are deleted. Nothing else in this repository changes.
contracts-chain takes an EXACT pin on publish ('1.0.0'), never a caret, for the reason its own
header gives: wallet, settlement, custody, indexer and now this service must agree byte for
byte on decimals. A pool that disagrees with the wallet about what a satoshi is credits a
miner the wrong number.
@cloudsforge/contracts-money arrived with micro-org#302, and it is the ONE dependency here
that takes 'link:' rather than 'file:'. A 'file:' path packs the dependency, and this package
declares its own dependency on contracts-chain with the 'workspace:^' protocol, which only
resolves inside the contracts workspace — packing it installs a package whose own dependency
cannot be found. micro-wallet's manifest records the same finding at greater length.
It is here because a payout is an entry in somebody else's double-entry ledger, and the entry
kind, the account purpose and the posting direction are that service's closed vocabulary. A
pool that hand-typed 'reward_granted' and 'available' as its own string literals would be a
second copy of a vocabulary that is exact-pinned precisely so there is only one.
There is deliberately NO @cloudsforge/contracts-events dependency and no outbox in this
release: nothing here publishes an event yet, and rule 9 says a repository declares what it
needs and nothing else. The first event this service has to emit is the payout, which is not
implemented — see the README.
tsx is a runtime dependency because the unpublished packages resolve to their TypeScript
sources. On publish their publishConfig points at dist/, tsx moves to devDependencies, and
the image runs 'node dist/index.js'.
@cloudsforge/auth arrived with micro-org#289 and its arrival did NOT make the read API
private. Every route that answers a question about work already done is still public, for the
reason src/server.ts gives at length: a miner's identity here is the stratum username they
typed into their own firmware, and gating the share history behind an estate login would make
it checkable by nobody. Exactly one route verifies a token — POST /v1/pool/ticket, which mints
the credential a BROWSER miner presents on the WebSocket transport, and which necessarily
requires an estate account because the account is the whole point of it. No scope is required
and no service token is accepted: it is a user route, and a user token is the only thing that
can name the user a mining ticket is minted for.
@cloudsforge/secrets arrived with micro-org#302 and it is used for ONE thing: validating the
shape of POOL_IDENTITY_CREDENTIAL, the long-lived credential the optional payout path
exchanges for a ledger service token. Nothing here signs anything even now — the mining ticket
is still a random opaque value matched by equality, not a MAC, and there is still no key to
fetch. The reason the check is not a local regex is that every obvious local rule refuses one
of the estate's two real credentials: a credential is 'cfsc_' + base64url, and measured live
on 2026-08-09 the testnet one contains a hyphen while the mainnet one does not.
